result.summary: Fixed numerous typos in outputstream.md (fileysystem/oll -> filesystem/all, intialized -> initialized, implmentation -> implementation, ClosedChannelExceptionn -> ClosedChannelException, outstaning -> outstanding, satisifed -> satisfied, preceeding -> preceding, unbuffer\" -> unbuffer, and a few other wording/punctuation fixes) matching HADOOP-18128.
result.notes: Work was already present uncommitted in the tree; verified completeness by grepping for all known typo strings (none remained) before committing.

result.summary: Documented the powershell(...) fencing method in both HDFSHighAvailabilityWithQJM.md and HDFSHighAvailabilityWithNFS.md, updating the 'two methods' count to three and adding a section describing usage and the process-identifier argument semantics matching PowerShellFencer's CommandLine-substring matching.
result.notes: No code changes were needed since PowerShellFencer already existed and worked; this requirement was purely documentation. hdfs-default.xml's dfs.ha.fencing.methods description remains generic and was left untouched since it does not enumerate specific methods.

result.summary: Updated CentralizedCacheManagement.md to correct the statement about SCM/pmem cache persistence, clarifying that dfs.datanode.pmem.cache.recovery=true enables recovery of previously cached data on DataNode restart, while leaving it false clears the SCM cache and requires re-caching.
result.notes: Docs-only change per requirement; the dfs.datanode.pmem.cache.recovery config property and its description were already documented elsewhere in the same file (likely added by a prior related HDFS-15533 change), so only the outdated summary bullet needed correction to reflect that SCM cache persistence is now supported.

result.summary: Removed the unused package-private JNStorage#getCurrentDir() accessor since no caller used it (all real usages call StorageDirectory#getCurrentDir() directly). No behavioral change to active JournalNode code paths.
result.notes: Verified via grep that no main or test code invoked JNStorage.getCurrentDir(); test/other usages matching the method name were all calls on StorageDirectory instances instead, so nothing else needed updating.

result.summary: HDFS-16602 targets the libhdfspp x-platform compatibility header that defines ssize_t on Windows; that header did not yet exist in this tree, so I created hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-native-client/src/main/native/libhdfspp/lib/x-platform/types.h directly in its post-HDFS-16602 form, using `#if defined(_WIN64)` / `#elif defined(_WIN32)` around `using ssize_t = __int64;` and `using ssize_t = long int;`. Header guard follows the existing x-platform convention (NATIVE_LIBHDFSPP_LIB_CROSS_PLATFORM_TYPES); no CMake change is needed since x-platform's CMakeLists only lists .cc sources.
result.notes: Dependency warning for the orchestrator: this slug is the follow-up to sibling slug `windows-ssize-t` (HDFS-16468, which originally creates this same types.h with the older `#ifdef _WIN64` / `#elif _WIN32` form). Per agent_plans/lanes.json the LIBHDFSPP lane runs `windows-ssize-t` AFTER this slug, so that agent will find types.h already present - it must NOT rewrite the preprocessor checks back to the bare `#ifdef`/`#elif _WIN32` form, only add the remaining HDFS-16468 pieces (e.g. `#include "x-platform/types.h"` in lib/fs/filehandle.h and a tests/x-platform/types_test.cc plus its CMake wiring). I deliberately kept my change to types.h only (no include wiring, no test) to stay in scope for HDFS-16602, which upstream was a two-line preprocessor fix.

result.summary: Removed redundant `strings.h` inclusions from fuse_dfs.h, configuration.cc, and configuration_loader.cc where no strings.h symbols were used directly, matching HDFS-16465. Added an explicit `#include <strings.h>` to fuse_init.c since it uses index() but previously depended on a transitive include from fuse_dfs.h. Left strings.h in fuse_trash.c and syscall_linux.cc since they genuinely use rindex()/strcasecmp().
result.notes: Scoped to hadoop-hdfs-native-client (fuse-dfs and libhdfspp), the only native HDFS client code under this tree that included strings.h. Verified no other transitive-include breakage by grepping all fuse-dfs source files for strings.h functions.
